Table of outliers and masking

Source: R/outlier.R
outlier_detect.Rd

outlier_detect() lists the flagged values (one row per subject x variable). outlier_mask() sets the listed values to NA.

Usage

outlier_detect(
  df,
  vars,
  id_col = NULL,
  rule = c("mad", "iqr", "both", "any"),
  mad_z_threshold = 3.5,
  iqr_k = 1.5,
  iqr_method = c("quantile", "hinges")
)

outlier_mask(df, outliers, id_col)

Arguments

df

A data frame.

vars

Numeric variables (names or tidyselect).

id_col

Identifier column (default: row numbers).

rule

Which values are listed: "mad" (MAD rule), "iqr" (Tukey), "both" (flagged by both rules, most conservative) or "any" (flagged by at least one rule).

mad_z_threshold

Cut-off of the modified z-score.

iqr_k

Multiplier of the Tukey fences.

iqr_method

"quantile" or "hinges", see outlier_flag_iqr().

outliers

Output of outlier_detect().

Value

outlier_detect(): a tibble id, Variable, Value, modified_z, MAD, IQR (logical: rule that flagged the value). outlier_mask(): df with the listed values set to NA.

Examples

out <- outlier_detect(cohort_sim, c(CRP_V0, NFL_V0), id_col = ID, rule = "any")
out
